question:
A 21-year-old man arrives at the Emergency Department after a window he was installing fell on him.
He reports left eye pain, blurred vision, and loss of vision in the lower portion of his left visual field. His
vital signs include a blood pressure of 148/84 mm Hg, heart rate of 88/min, respiratory rate of 15/min,
and temperature of 36.9■ (98.4■). Physical examination reveals multiple superficial lacerations on the
face, arms, and legs. The right eye shows a superficial upper eyelid laceration. Examination of the left
eye reveals conjunctival hyperemia, a peaked pupil, iridial asymmetry, hyphema, and vitreous
hemorrhage. The fundus is difficult to visualize due to the vitreous hemorrhage. Visual acuity is 20/25
in the right eye but cannot be accurately assessed in the left eye. What is the next best step in
managing this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Administration of oral antibiotics and monitoring for
intraocular pressure changes (B) Examination of the left eye with fluorescein (C) Placement of an
ocular shield and outpatient ophthalmology follow-up (D) Immediate CT scan of the orbits and systemic
antibiotic administration (E) Emergent surgical intervention without antibiotic administration (F) Use of a
slit lamp to evaluate for corneal abrasions prior to ophthalmology consultation (G) Systemic
administration of vancomycin and emergent ophthalmology consultation (H) Placement of an ocular
pad and emergent ophthalmology consultation (I) Administration of IV dexamethasone and delayed
ophthalmology consultation (J) Administration of topical corticosteroids and emergent ophthalmology
consultation
 A. Emergent surgical intervention without antibiotic administration

B. Administration of oral antibiotics and monitoring for intraocular pressure changes
C. Use of a slit lamp to evaluate for corneal abrasions prior to ophthalmology consultation
D. Immediate CT scan of the orbits and systemic antibiotic administration
E. Administration of topical corticosteroids and emergent ophthalmology consultation
F. Examination of the left eye with fluorescein
G. Administration of IV dexamethasone and delayed ophthalmology consultation
H. Systemic administration of vancomycin and emergent ophthalmology consultation
I. Placement of an ocular shield and outpatient ophthalmology follow-up
J. Placement of an ocular pad and emergent ophthalmology consultation
